Ok so I started looking into how to make the notification swipeable when the player is not playing. The [issue](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/12872204/how-to-cancel-a-foreground-service-from-using-the-notification-swipe-dismiss-o#35721582) I found is that notifications with a *foreground service* running can never be swiped away. If I remove the `startForeground()` line everything works fine, since what a foreground service does is only telling the user not to kill that app since it is currently producing something for the user.

So what should I do? I could think of these options:
- keep the foreground service running only while the player is playing, otherwise stop it. This would provide the behaviour of other players, but has a downside: while a stream is paused [the Android system could decide](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Service#stopForeground(boolean)) he needs memory and kill NewPipe.
- do not change anything, thus not implementing any swiping at all

What do you think? @cool-student @opusforlife2 @avently @wb9688 @TobiGr @B0pol

> while a stream is paused the Android system could decide he needs memory and kill NewPipe.

This is perfectly fine. This is how other media players behave as well.

< What do you think?

Of course to leave it as is (non-swipeable perpetual notification). As a user I don't want to see how the app is killed by Android. There is no problem at all with the notification displayed all the time. It allows to start and pause playback from notification while browsing other apps. Without notification it is impossible and I need to visit the app again, to wait some time once it reloads a stream, to replay it again.
With auto play disabled the notification is disabled too currently once the user presses pause.

> With auto play disabled the notification is disabled too currently once the user presses pause.

Yes, but for the main player only. Not the background and popup players. And the popup case is still fine because you can drag it down to the X to close it no matter what screen or app you are on.

That leaves the background player. If you select "Close" as one of the 5 action buttons, you can tap that to close it. But if "Close" is not one of your 5 action buttons, then you have no way of closing the stream from the notification shade. You'd either have to open the queue from the notification, and swipe the stream away, or you'd have to open the app, and close the video from the main player's close button.

The deleteIntent behaviour is only applicable to the case where "Close" is _not_ one of your 5 action buttons. So the notification will be permanently non-swipe-able if you keep "Close" as one of your buttons.

In particular, [`onSwipeToDismiss`](https://github.com/aosp-mirror/platform_frameworks_base/commit/afae4e715fcda3865938641de22f124bba6fba90#diff-f81c7625ea336cd98f1b40ad94ca0f84R598-R603) is [called](https://github.com/aosp-mirror/platform_frameworks_base/commit/afae4e715fcda3865938641de22f124bba6fba90#diff-bb06bfe74ba9f5d3d8ff45bf7ad7a1c3R134-R135) when the last item on the media carousel is swiped away, and what it does is only [making the media sessions inactive](https://github.com/aosp-mirror/platform_frameworks_base/blob/afae4e715fcda3865938641de22f124bba6fba90/packages/SystemUI/src/com/android/systemui/media/MediaDataManager.kt#L277-L290), which according to the [javadoc](https://github.com/aosp-mirror/platform_frameworks_base/blob/afae4e715fcda3865938641de22f124bba6fba90/packages/SystemUI/src/com/android/systemui/media/MediaDataManager.kt#L278) is the same as what happens when the player has been paused for a while. Therefore the effect of swiping the notification and that of timing out is exactly the same, meaning there is no way to distinguish between them and act accordingly (i.e. close the player only if the notification was swiped, but not on time out). Afaik currently NewPipe completely ignores the active state change of the media session (i.e. `mediaSession.addOnActiveChangeListener` is never called), since we do not want to release the player even after a while, as that would delete the queue.
*Please note that all of what I said above could be completely wrong, as I had never read AOSP code before.*
